title: Neck osteoarthritis, frailty and balance when looking down (UK)

direct_answer: Neck osteoarthritis can cause stiffness that makes looking down at steps or turning the head harder. With frailty, this can affect balance. Good lighting, clear floors, handrails and gentle neck and balance exercises can help.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member

content:
Turning or tipping your head is part of walking safely.

This guide covers practical tips. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Why it matters

Stiff necks make it harder to check your feet, steps and surroundings.

Safety tips

  • Good lighting.
  • Contrasting step edges.
  • Handrails.
  • Turn your whole body rather than just your head.

Exercises

A physiotherapist can suggest gentle neck movements and balance exercises.

When to seek help

See your GP for persistent neck pain or new dizziness.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for sudden weakness, numbness, slurred speech or loss of balance, which can be signs of a stroke.
  • Get urgent advice for neck pain with fever, or numbness or weakness in arms or legs.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can neck arthritis cause dizziness?

Dizziness has many causes; get it checked.

Is a collar useful?

Usually not long term.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Neck pain
  • NHS: Balance exercises
